title: Additive and scalar operations on dual-number tangent vectors.
statement: theorem tangentVectors_operations (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) : let K := X.residueField x let D := Spec (.of (DualNumber K)) let E := Spec (.of (TrivSqZeroExt K (Fin 2 → K))) let b := X.fromSpecResidueField x let c : Spec K ⟶ D := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom K K K).toRingHom) let q : D ⟶ Spec K := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.inlHom K K)) let j : Fin 2 → (D ⟶ E) := fun i => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.map (LinearMap.proj i : (Fin 2 → K) →ₗ[K] K)).toRingHom) let s : D ⟶ E := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.map ((LinearMap.proj 0 : (Fin 2 → K) →ₗ[K] K) + LinearMap.proj 1)).toRingHom) let m : K → (D ⟶ D) := fun t => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.map (t • (LinearMap.id : K →ₗ[K] K))).toRingHom) let T := {θ : D ⟶ X // c ≫ θ = b ∧ θ ≫ p = q ≫ b ≫ p} ∃ a : AddCommGroup T, letI := a; ∃ v : Module K T, letI := v; (0 : T).val = q ≫ b ∧ (∀ θ₁ θ₂ : T, ∀ Θ : E ⟶ X, j 0 ≫ Θ = θ₁.val → j 1 ≫ Θ = θ₂.val → (θ₁ + θ₂).val = s ≫ Θ) ∧ (∀ (t : K) (θ : T), (t • θ).val = m t ≫ θ.val)

proof.text: For a field K and a based scheme map b:Spec K→X over any scheme Y, define the tangent-vector subtype by its point and structure-map triangles. Prove functoriality of the square-zero coordinate maps and their compatibility with the point and projection maps by ring-homomorphism extensionality and the Spec composition law.

Apply the finite-copy dual-number extension theorem for n=2 to obtain the unique gluing of two tangent vectors. Define addition by precomposition with the sum-of-coordinates map. Its point triangle follows from a coordinate restriction; its structure-map triangle follows by applying uniqueness to the common constant family in Y. Define scalar multiplication by coefficient scaling, and zero by the constant map. All operations satisfy both triangles.

The gluing of scale(r,a) and scale(t,a) is induced by the linear map z↦(rz,tz). Its sum restriction is scale(r+t,a). This proves additivity in the scalar, the two additive zero laws, and the inverse law with scalars -1 and 1. Exchanging coordinates of the two-copy gluing proves additive commutativity by uniqueness.

Glue a,d,e using the finite-copy extension theorem for n=3. Coordinate selection identifies their pairwise gluings with restrictions of this same three-copy gluing. Grouping its first two or last two coordinates identifies the two iterated sums with precomposition by (z0,z1,z2)↦z0+z1+z2; equality of the linear maps proves associativity.

Scaling both coordinates of the two-copy gluing identifies the gluing of scale(t,a),scale(t,d). Equality of the linear maps t(z0+z1)=tz0+tz1 proves distributivity. Composition of scaling maps proves the multiplicative scalar law, and the identity and zero maps prove the remaining scalar laws.

Assemble the explicit operations and proved identities into AddCommGroup and Module structures, with the recursive natural and integer actions. Specialize K to the residue field and b to fromSpecResidueField. Zero and scalar formulas hold definitionally. Unique gluing proves the addition formula for every morphism Θ with the two prescribed restrictions.
